Return fact number 1 in reading order (counting from 1) as a JSON object with exactly these fields:
- "subject": the entity the fact is about, as written in the text

- "object": the other entity as written (object_kind "entity"), or a literal value (object_kind "literal"); an acquisition price is "USD <integer>", like "USD 2100000000"
- "object_kind": "entity" or "literal"
- "qualifier": "EXACT", "APPROX" ("about"), "UPPER_BOUND" ("up to"), "LOWER_BOUND" ("at least"), or "NONE" when the fact has no amount
- "polarity": "ASSERTED", "DENIED", "HYPOTHETICAL" or "REPORTED"
- "quote": the exact words of the text the fact rests on, copied character for character
- "start", "end": character offsets of the quote in the text, so that text[start:end] == quote
- "valid_from", "valid_to": "YYYY-MM-DD" dates the text gives for when the fact held, else null

When the text has fewer than 1 facts, answer with predicate "NONE", empty strings for subject, object and quote, object_kind "literal", qualifier "NONE", polarity "ASSERTED", start 0, end 0 and null dates. Answer with predicate "CANNOT_COMPLY" when you cannot do the task.
